info.description:
HTTP API of the oracle, started with `oracle api`.
The server listens on `PORT` (default 8080) and connects to Postgres before it starts listening: if the database is unreachable, the process exits and nothing answers.
There is no authentication. Routes that don't exist answer 404, and known routes called with the wrong method answer 405 with an `Allow` header, both in plain text.
info.title: oracle API

get.description:
Reports that the server is up, with the current server time in UTC (RFC 3339).
The database connection is checked once at startup, not on every call, so a 200 means the process is running and was able to connect when it started.
No side effects; safe to call repeatedly, for example from a load balancer or monitor.

405.description: Method Not Allowed: only GET and HEAD are accepted (Allow: GET, HEAD)

get.description:
The plan of oracle recommend for the session after the latest one: which stocks to buy, how many and at what prices, ranked by track record and analyst upside.
Tiers are tried from strongest to weakest: the plan stops at the first unless fill is true. Analyst targets come from Yahoo Finance, an unofficial API: when it fails the plan ranks by history only (analyst_estimates is false), and targets that take too long are left for a later call.

get.description:
Every stock traded on the latest session whose close fires the rule of the tier, with its order prices and track record: the candidates oracle recommend picks from, before analyst targets and position sizing.
Eligible stocks come first, then by expectancy. An empty list means no signal in that tier.

get.description:
The parameters of the swing rule that oracle recommend and oracle backtest use. Prices are set from the ATR (average true range of 14 sessions) of the signal day.
A signal is a close above the 200-day average with RSI(2) below oversold. The tiers lower the bar for oversold; see /strategy/tiers.

The signal levels, from strongest to weakest. oracle recommend stops at the first that fills the list, or goes down the tiers with -fill.
Labels are in Portuguese, as the CLI prints them; the tier query parameter also accepts them without accents (medio, tendencia).

Every ticker with quotes in the database, of any spec (stocks, real estate funds, ETFs, BDRs), in ticker order.
Name, spec and ISIN come from the latest quote of each ticker. An empty database answers an empty list.
Summary of one ticker and its latest quote. The ticker is case-insensitive.

Runs the rule on the last years of one stock, as oracle recommend does for every stock: whether there is a signal on its latest session, the order prices, and its track record.
Only the part of the series after the last split counts. Without at least 260 sessions there, or with a median volume below min_volume, the track record is empty and there is no signal.

The trades behind the track record of /tickers/{ticker}/analysis, in date order: each signal is bought with a limit order the next session and sold at the target, the stop or the close of the last holding session.
